# Minimal ArmO3CPU + CHAOSPhysReg smoke config for the SDC research framework.
# Runs a user-supplied AArch64 static binary; injects ONE bit-flip into a
# (by default random) physical integer register at firstClock, traces reads.
#
# Usage:
#   build/ARM/gem5.opt o3_chaos_smoke.py --binary ./movbe_kernel --iters 200 \
#       --phys-idx -1 --bits 1
import sys, os
import m5
from m5.objects import *

thispath = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))

class L1ICache(Cache):
    assoc = 4; size = "32KiB"; tag_latency = 2; data_latency = 2
    response_latency = 2; mshrs = 4; tgts_per_mshr = 20
    def connectCPU(self, cpu): self.cpu_side = cpu.icache_port
    def connectBus(self, bus): self.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports

class L1DCache(Cache):
    assoc = 4; size = "32KiB"; tag_latency = 2; data_latency = 2
    response_latency = 2; mshrs = 4; tgts_per_mshr = 20
    def connectCPU(self, cpu): self.cpu_side = cpu.dcache_port
    def connectBus(self, bus): self.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports

class L2Cache(Cache):
    assoc = 8; size = "256KiB"; tag_latency = 20; data_latency = 20
    response_latency = 20; mshrs = 20; tgts_per_mshr = 12
    def connectCPUSideBus(self, bus): self.cpu_side = bus.mem_side_ports
    def connectMemSideBus(self, bus): self.mem_side = bus.cpu_side_ports

bin_default = os.path.join(thispath, "movbe_kernel")
opts = m5.options
from m5.util import addToPath
import argparse
ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument("--binary", default=bin_default)
ap.add_argument("--iters", default="200")
ap.add_argument("--phys-idx", default="-1", help="-1 = random phys reg")
ap.add_argument("--arch-idx", default="0", help="arch reg idx (arch modes)")
ap.add_argument("--mode", default="phys", help="phys|arch_frontend|arch_commit")
ap.add_argument("--reg-class", default="integer", help="integer|floating_point|vector|both")
ap.add_argument("--bits", default="1", help="bits to flip")
ap.add_argument("--mask", default="0", help="bitmask; 0=random(bits)")
ap.add_argument("--fault", default="bit_flip", help="bit_flip|stuck_at_zero|stuck_at_one|random")
ap.add_argument("--first-clock", default="100000", help="cycle of single injection")
ap.add_argument("--max-faults", default="1")
ap.add_argument("--probability", default="1.0", help="per-interval injection probability (use <1 with maxFaults>1 to spread injections in time)")
ap.add_argument("--seed", default="0")
ap.add_argument("--no-fi", action="store_true", help="disable injection (golden run)")
ap.add_argument("--max-tick", default="0", help="0 = no cap; else cap sim (Root.max_tick)")
ap.add_argument("--lsq-fwd-prob", default="0.0", help="CHAOSLSQFwd per-forward corruption probability (0=off)")
ap.add_argument("--lsq-fwd-bits", default="1", help="bits to flip on forwarded data")
ap.add_argument("--lsq-fwd-byte", default="-1", help="byte offset in forwarded buffer (-1=random)")
# P-D1: structural (whole-word) fault axis for CHAOSLSQFwd. Orthogonal to the
# per-byte bit-fault above. Models core-179 D1 (byte-lane skew / all-zero) which
# is NOT expressible as a bit flip (MICROARCH_SUPplement §2.2).
ap.add_argument("--lsq-structural", default="none", help="none|byte_lane_skew|all_zero (P-D1)")
ap.add_argument("--lsq-skew", default="0", help="byte_lane_skew rotation 1..7 (0=random)")
# P-D2: address-path (D2) injector — zeroes a byte of the load effAddr
# presented to the MMU. Models core 179's D2 (0814/0824: arch MSB != MMU MSB).
ap.add_argument("--addr-prob", default="0.0", help="CHAOSAddrPath per-load addr-corruption prob (0=off)")
ap.add_argument("--addr-byte", default="7", help="which byte of effAddr to zero (7=MSB,-1=random)")
# P-D3: PTW readout (D3) injector — bit-flips fetched PTEs. H7 knob: ptwEcc.
ap.add_argument("--ptw-prob", default="0.0", help="CHAOSPTW per-descriptor-fetch flip prob (0=off)")
ap.add_argument("--ptw-bits", default="1", help="bits to flip per PTE")
ap.add_argument("--ptw-ecc", action="store_true", help="model PTW array ECC (H7: corrects single-bit)")

ap.add_argument("--l1d", default="32KiB")
a = ap.parse_args()

system = System()
system.clk_domain = SrcClockDomain()
system.clk_domain.clock = "2GHz"
system.clk_domain.voltage_domain = VoltageDomain()
system.mem_mode = "timing"
system.mem_ranges = [AddrRange("512MiB")]

system.cpu = ArmO3CPU()
# Larger OoO window — mirrors the ARM64 "big ROB/PRF" thesis in cpu.md.
system.cpu.numROBEntries = 192
system.cpu.LQEntries = 32
system.cpu.SQEntries = 32
system.cpu.numPhysIntRegs = 256
system.cpu.numPhysFloatRegs = 256

system.cpu.icache = L1ICache()
system.cpu.dcache = L1DCache()
system.cpu.icache.connectCPU(system.cpu)
system.cpu.dcache.connectCPU(system.cpu)
system.l2bus = L2XBar()
system.cpu.icache.connectBus(system.l2bus)
system.cpu.dcache.connectBus(system.l2bus)
system.l2cache = L2Cache()
system.l2cache.connectCPUSideBus(system.l2bus)
system.membus = SystemXBar()
system.l2cache.connectMemSideBus(system.membus)
system.cpu.createInterruptController()
system.system_port = system.membus.cpu_side_ports
system.mem_ctrl = MemCtrl()
system.mem_ctrl.dram = DDR3_1600_8x8()
system.mem_ctrl.dram.range = system.mem_ranges[0]
system.mem_ctrl.port = system.membus.mem_side_ports

system.workload = SEWorkload.init_compatible(a.binary)
process = Process()
process.cmd = [a.binary, a.iters]
system.cpu.workload = process
system.cpu.createThreads()

if not a.no_fi:
    system.fi = CHAOSPhysReg(
        cpu=system.cpu,
        injectionMode=a.mode,
        targetPhysRegIdx=int(a.phys_idx),
        targetArchRegIdx=int(a.arch_idx),
        regTargetClass=a.reg_class,
        probability=float(a.probability),
        bitsToChange=int(a.bits),
        faultMask=int(a.mask, 0),

#!/bin/bash
# H6: D1 vs D2 spectrum separability (single/multi-defect arbiter, sim-side proxy)
# 2x2 design: {D1 on/off} x {D2 on/off}, measure {crash, SDC, benign}
# Falsifiable: if D1-only and D2-only spectra indistinguishable -> single-defect
#
# Reproducibility note (adversarial-review fix): this script no longer hardcodes
# /home/sdc/vmcore/...; it resolves paths relative to itself and sources the
# user-space build env (~/gem5-deps/env.sh) so gem5.opt's libprotobuf/libabsl
# are found via LD_LIBRARY_PATH (the binary has no rpath).
set -e
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"          # gem5-fi repo root
GEM5="$REPO/CHAOS/gem5/build/ARM/gem5.opt"
PROBE="$HERE/ptrskew_kernel"
CFG="$HERE/o3_chaos_smoke.py"
# Source user-space build env if present (sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH so gem5.opt runs).
[ -f "$HOME/gem5-deps/env.sh" ] && source "$HOME/gem5-deps/env.sh"
# Optional CPU isolation list (defaults to all cpus if /tmp/cpus.txt absent).
CPUS="$(cat /tmp/cpus.txt 2>/dev/null || nproc)"
mkdir -p /tmp/h6
run() {
  local tag=$1; shift
  local out=/tmp/h6/$tag
  timeout 200 taskset -c "$CPUS" "$GEM5" -d "$out" "$CFG" \
    --binary "$PROBE" --iters 500 --no-fi --seed 42 --max-faults 50 \
    --first-clock 2000 "$@" 2>&1 | grep -E 'fails|Page table fault|Exiting|panic' | head -3
  echo "  [stats] $(grep -E 'numStructuralByteLaneSkew|numAddrFaults|numFaultsInjected|numHooksCalled' $out/stats.txt 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
}
echo "=== H6: D1 vs D2 spectrum separability ==="
echo "[1/4] baseline (no FI):"
run baseline
echo "[2/4] D1-only (byte_lane_skew prob=0.05):"
run D1_only --lsq-fwd-prob 0.05 --lsq-structural byte_lane_skew --lsq-skew 1
echo "[3/4] D2-only (addr byte7-zero prob=0.05):"
run D2_only --addr-prob 0.05 --addr-byte 7
echo "[4/4] D1+D2 (both prob=0.05):"
run D1D2 --lsq-fwd-prob 0.05 --lsq-structural byte_lane_skew --lsq-skew 1 --addr-prob 0.05 --addr-byte 7

计划已完成并保存到 `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-02-positional-parity-research.md`。

## 计划核心内容

**三层递进架构**（8 个 Task，每个一个 commit，分支 `research/posparity-core179`）：

| Task | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | 三启示逐一论证（fail-fast / 位置锚定校验 / PEPR 三级防线），每条按“合理性/必要性/可行性 + 反方正面处理 + 置信标注”三维展开，文献锚点已在计划撰写期核实（[PEPR ITC'22](https://wadmes.github.io/cv/raw/ITC22.pdf)、[Google/Stanford 10× test escapes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01786)、[Intel IFS/SBAF](https://docs.kernel.org/arch/x86/ifs.html)等） |
| 4–5 | **CHAOSPosParity 验证原型**：镜像 CHAOSLSQFwd 的 SimObject 模式，挂在 `lsq_unit.cc:1499` 同一转发点，构成“注入侧-检测侧”闭环实验回路；2×4×2 检出率矩阵 × 5 seeds |
| 6 | 理论开销：位开销（32/64=50%，可缩减至 8/64=12.5%）、门数、时序深度、与 ECC/DMR 对比 |
| 7–8 | 总裁决成文 + 索引收尾 |

## 撰写期已完成的实证勘察（计划可信度的基础）

- **实验回路验证可用**：ptrskew 探针本机 gcc 静态重建成功；golden run `fails=0`；`--lsq-structural byte_lane_skew` 注入后复现 `panic: Page table fault`（D1 链完整）。
- **一个重要的计划期理论发现**：论文 §6.2 设想的“位置标签”若用**纯 XOR 聚合**，对字节旋转是**置换不变的**（`W'⊕W=0`）——检出率为 0。这与“ECC 对汉明 0 旋转盲视”是同一数学根源。计划已修正为非交换混合（按通道 mod-256 加法加权），并把这一推导本身作为报告的核心理论贡献。逐字节位置常量 `L_i=(i+1)&7` 的双射性保证任意 `ror_k` 旋转 100% 必失配。
- 用户原文“物理干燥区域”判断为 PEPR（physically-aware region，“物理感知区域”）之误，按 PEPR 本义处理。

**两种执行方式：**

**1. Subagent-Driven（推荐）** — 每个 Task 派发独立 subagent，任务间双阶段审查，迭代快

**2. Inline Execution** — 用 executing-plans 在本会话内按检查点批量执行

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];

    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];

    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## The Process

```dot

    rankdir=TB;

    subgraph cluster_per_task {
        label="Per Task";

        "Fix round R of 5: R≤3 resume implementer; R≥4 fresh implementer, more capable model" [shape=box];

    }

    "Generate review package, dispatch task reviewer (./task-reviewer-prompt.md)" -> "Spec ✅ and quality approved?";

    "Adjudicate each open finding" -> "Any load-bearing finding?";
    "Any load-bearing finding?" -> "STOP: report BLOCKED to human partner" [label="yes"];
    "Any load-bearing finding?" -> "Park findings in ledger with rulings" [label="no"];
    "Park findings in ledger with rulings" -> "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete";
    "Append completion to ledger, mark todo complete" -> "More tasks remain?";

    "More tasks remain?" -> "Dispatch final code reviewer (../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md)" [label="no"];
    "Dispatch final code reviewer (../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md)" -> "Final findings? ONE fix dispatch, one scoped re-review, adjudicate residuals";

```

## Setup

Ensure the work happens in an isolated workspace: use
superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one.
Never start implementation on a main/master branch without your human
partner's explicit consent.

Conversation memory does not survive compaction. In real sessions,
controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task
sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. Track progress in
a ledger file, not only in todos.

- Each plan owns a workspace: at skill start, run this skill's
  `scripts/sdd-workspace PLAN_FILE` — it prints the plan's git-ignored
  directory (`<repo-root>/.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/`), home to
  every artifact for THIS plan: ledger, briefs, reports, review packages.
  Another plan's directory is never yours to read or write.
- Check for this plan's ledger at `<workspace>/progress.md`. If its first
  line names your plan file, tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are DONE
  — do not re-dispatch them; resume at the first task without one. A task
  whose last line is a fix round is mid-loop: resume the loop at the next
  round. A ledger whose first line names a different plan file — or a stray
  ledger at the old flat path `.superpowers/sdd/progress.md` — is another
  plan's progress: leave it in place and start your own, fresh.
- Create the ledger with its identity as the first line:
  `# SDD ledger — plan: <plan file path>`.
- The ledger is your recovery map: the commits it names exist in git even
  when your context no longer remembers creating them. After compaction,
  trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
- `git clean -fdx` will destroy the workspace (it's git-ignored scratch); if
  that happens, recover from `git log`.

Read the plan once, note its context and Global Constraints, and create a
todo per task.

Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts:

- tasks that contradict each other or the plan's Global Constraints
- anything the plan explicitly mandates that the review rubric treats as a
  defect (a test that asserts nothing, verbatim duplication of a logic block)

Present everything you find to your human partner as one batched question —
each finding beside the plan text that mandates it, asking which governs —
before execution begins, not one interrupt per discovery mid-plan. If the
scan is clean, proceed without comment. The review loop remains the net for
conflicts that only emerge from implementation.

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture and design tasks**: use the most capable available model.
The final whole-branch review is one of these — dispatch it on the most
capable available model, not the session default.

**Review tasks**: choose the model with the same judgment, scaled to the
diff's size, complexity, and risk. A small mechanical diff does not need the
most capable model; a subtle concurrency change does. Scoped re-reviews of
small fix diffs take a cheap-to-mid tier.

**Fix-loop escalation (rounds 4-5)**: use a model at least one tier above
the implementer that got stuck.

**Always specify the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent.** An
omitted model inherits your session's model — often the most capable and
most expensive — which silently defeats this section.

**Turn count beats token price.** Wall-clock and context cost scale with how
many turns a subagent takes, and the cheapest models routinely take 2-3× the
turns on multi-step work — costing more overall. Use a mid-tier model as the
floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose descriptions.
When the task's plan text contains the complete code to write, the
implementation is transcription plus testing: use the cheapest tier for
that implementer. Single-file mechanical fixes also take the cheapest tier.

**Task complexity signals (implementation tasks):**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## The Task Loop

Everything you paste into a dispatch prompt — and everything a subagent
prints back — stays resident in your context for the rest of the session
and is re-read on every later turn. Hand artifacts over as files.

### 1. Dispatch the implementer

Record BASE (`git rev-parse HEAD`) before dispatching — the review package
and fix-round diffs need it.

- **Task brief:** before dispatching an implementer, run this skill's
  `scripts/task-brief PLAN_FILE N` — it extracts the task's full text to a
  uniquely named file and prints the path. Compose the dispatch so the
  brief stays the single source of
  requirements. Your dispatch should contain: (1) one line on where this
  task fits in the project; (2) the brief path, introduced as "read this
  first — it is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim";
  (3) interfaces and decisions from earlier tasks that the brief cannot
  know; (4) your resolution of any ambiguity you noticed in the brief;
  (5) the report-file path and report contract. Exact values (numbers,
  magic strings, signatures, test cases) appear only in the brief. Never
  make a subagent read the whole plan file.
- **Report file:** name the implementer's report file after the brief
  (brief `…/task-N-brief.md` → report `…/task-N-report.md`) and put it in
  the dispatch prompt. The implementer writes the full report there and
  returns only status, commits, a one-line test summary, and concerns.
- A dispatch prompt describes one task, not the session's history. Do not
  paste accumulated prior-task summaries ("state after Tasks 1-3") into
  later dispatches — a real session's dispatch hit 42k chars of which 99%
  was pasted history. A fresh subagent needs its task, the interfaces it
  touches, and the global constraints. Nothing else.
- If an earlier task parked a finding in the area this task touches, carry
  a pointer to that ledger entry in the dispatch.
- Record the implementer's agent identity from the dispatch result —
  fix-loop rounds 1-3 resume this agent.
- Never dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts).

Template: [implementer-prompt.md](implementer-prompt.md)

### 2. Handle the report

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Generate the review package (`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD`, from this skill's directory — it prints the unique file path it wrote; BASE is the commit you recorded before dispatching the implementer — never `HEAD~1`, which silently drops all but the last commit of a multi-commit task), then dispatch the task reviewer with the printed path.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

If the implementer asks questions — before starting or mid-task — answer
clearly and completely, provide additional context if needed, and don't
rush it into implementation.

### 3. Review the task

Per-task reviews are task-scoped gates. The broad review happens once, at the
final whole-branch review. Never skip the task review, and never accept a
report missing either verdict — spec compliance AND task quality are both
required. Implementer self-review never replaces the task review; both are
needed.

- Hand the reviewer its diff as a file: run this skill's
  `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD` and pass the reviewer the file path
  it prints (or, without bash: `git log --oneline`, `git diff --stat`,
  and `git diff -U10` for the range, redirected to one uniquely named
  file). The output never enters your own context, and the reviewer sees
  the commit list, stat summary, and full diff with context in one Read
  call. Use the BASE you recorded before dispatching the implementer —
  never `HEAD~1`, which silently truncates multi-commit tasks. Never
  dispatch a task reviewer without a diff file.
- **Reviewer inputs:** the task reviewer gets three paths — the same brief
  file, the report file, and the review package — plus the global
  constraints that bind the task.
- The global-constraints block you hand the reviewer is its attention
  lens. Copy the binding requirements verbatim from the plan's Global
  Constraints section or the spec: exact values, exact formats, and the
  stated relationships between components ("same layout as X", "matches
  Y"). The reviewer's template already carries the process rules (YAGNI,
  test hygiene, review method) — the constraints block is for what THIS
  project's spec demands.
- Do not add open-ended directives like "check all uses" or "run race tests
  if useful" without a concrete, task-specific reason
- Do not ask a reviewer to re-run tests the implementer already ran on the
  same code — the implementer's report carries the test evidence
- Do not pre-judge findings for the reviewer — never instruct a reviewer to
  ignore or not flag a specific issue. If you believe a finding would be a
  false positive, let the reviewer raise it and adjudicate it in the review
  loop. If the prompt you are writing contains "do not flag," "don't treat X
  as a defect," "at most Minor," or "the plan chose" — stop: you are
  pre-judging, usually to spare yourself a review loop.
The task reviewer may report "⚠️ Cannot verify from diff" items — requirements
that live in unchanged code or span tasks. These do not block the rest of the
review, but you must resolve each one yourself before marking the task
complete: you hold the plan and cross-task context the reviewer
lacks. If you confirm an item is a real gap, treat it as a failed spec
review — it enters the fix loop with the other findings.

Template: [task-reviewer-prompt.md](task-reviewer-prompt.md)

### 4. The fix loop

The loop triggers when the review reports spec ❌, any Critical or Important
finding, or a ⚠️ item you confirmed as a real gap.

Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:

- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
  never enter the loop.
- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with
  what the plan's text requires — is the human's decision, like any plan
  contradiction: present the finding and the plan text, ask which governs.
  Do not dismiss the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not
  dispatch a fix that contradicts the plan without asking.
Everything else enters the loop. A fix round is one fix dispatch plus one
scoped re-review. Five rounds maximum per task:

**Rounds 1-3 — resume the original implementer.** Send it the open findings
verbatim. Its context is intact: it knows the task, the code, and its own
choices. If your harness cannot send another message to a live subagent,
dispatch a fresh implementer carrying the brief path, the report-file path,
and the findings — the report file is the persistent memory either way.

**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh implementer on a more capable model** (per
Model Selection), with the brief path, the report-file path, the open
findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this task
[N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A loop
that survives three resumes usually means the implementer cannot see its
own problem — fresh eyes and a capability bump in one move.

**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. Name the
covering test files in the fix message — a one-line fix does not need the
whole suite.

**The re-review is scoped.** Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
each finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED and flags new breakage in the fix
diff only. New Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open
findings list. Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred
minors — they never extend the loop.

**After each round,** append to the ledger:
`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`

Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays
clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review.

**The breaker.** When round 5's re-review still leaves findings open, stop
dispatching. Adjudicate each open finding yourself — you hold the plan and
the cross-task context the reviewer lacks:

- **The reviewer is wrong, or the point is contestable:** park it —
  `Task <N>: parked — <finding> — ruling: <why the code stands>`. The final
  review sees both sides.
- **Real, but nothing downstream builds on it:** park it the same way, with
  a ruling that says it's real and deferred.
- **Real and load-bearing** — a later task builds on it, or it reveals a
  plan defect: STOP. Append `Task <N>: BLOCKED — <reason>` and report to
  your human partner with the finding, the plan text it collides with, and
  the fix history. Parking a structural failure lets every dependent task
  build on it and hands the final review a problem it cannot fix either.

Adjudicate only at the cap. Adjudicating earlier to end a loop is
pre-judging with a different name. Every adjudication is a ledger entry —
a silent discard is forbidden.

### 5. Complete the task

When the review comes back clean — or every open finding is parked with a
ruling at the cap — append the completion line to the ledger in the same
message as your other bookkeeping:

- `Task <N>: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, review clean)`
- `Task <N>: complete (commits <base7>..<head7>, <K> parked)` after a
  tripped breaker

Then mark the todo complete and move on. Never move to the next task while
the review has open Critical/Important issues that are neither fixed nor
parked-with-ruling at the cap.

## Final Review

The final whole-branch review gets a package too: run
`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD` (MERGE_BASE = the commit the
branch started from, e.g. `git merge-base main HEAD`) and include the
printed path in the final review dispatch, so the final reviewer reads
one file instead of re-deriving the branch diff with git commands. Dispatch
on the most capable available model (see Model Selection), using
superpowers:requesting-code-review's
[code-reviewer.md](../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md). Point it at
the ledger's deferred-minor and parked lines so it can triage which must be
fixed before merge.

If the final whole-branch review returns findings, dispatch ONE fix subagent
with the complete findings list — not one fixer per finding.
Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real
session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.
Then run exactly one scoped re-review of the fix wave
(`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD` over the fix range,
[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md)).
Adjudicate any residual findings as in the task loop's breaker: park with
rulings, or stop on load-bearing ones. There is no second fix wave —
residual load-bearing findings surface to your human partner when
finishing-a-development-branch presents the options.

## Finish

When the final whole-branch review is clean and its fixes are merged,
delete this plan's workspace (`rm -rf <workspace>`) — the git history is
the record now. Sibling directories belong to other plans; leave them
alone.

Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Close enough on spec compliance" | Reviewer found spec gaps = not done. Fix or hit the cap and adjudicate — those are the only exits. |
| "I'll fix it myself, dispatching is overhead" | Controller fixes pollute your context and skip review. Resume the implementer. |
| "One more round will converge" | Past the cap, rounds don't converge — the failure is structural. Adjudicate and route. |
| "The reviewer will just find something new anyway" | Scoped re-reviews verify fixes; they cannot wander. New findings on untouched code go to the ledger, not the loop. |
| "This finding is obviously wrong, I'll drop it" | You adjudicate only at the cap, and every ruling is a ledger entry. Silent discards are forbidden. |
| "The fix was small, skip the re-review" | Unreviewed fixes are how regressions land. Every round ends with a scoped re-review. |
| "Reviews slow the loop down" | The loop without reviews is just unverified churn. Reviews are the loop's brakes and steering. |
| "Ledger bookkeeping is overhead" | The ledger is what survives compaction. Controllers without one have re-dispatched entire completed task sequences. |

我阅读了所有三个评审文件，对照已提交的 blob（与工作树字节完全相同）验证了 git 机制，对照仓库源文件（paper_zh.md, DIAGNOSIS_REPORT.md, 08-14/08-26 vmcore 报告, MICROARCH_SUPPLEMENT.md, readme.md）检查了案例事实，并独立重新获取了外部引用（4 篇 arXiv 论文中的 3 篇下载了全文 PDF 并进行了文本提取，mcelog 页面，内核 boot-options，docs.kernel.org，DBLP API 查询，DOI 解析，以及 usenix 404 复现）。

## (1) 规范符合性：✅（有一个小瑕疵）

已符合：
- **骨架完全匹配**：所有 15 个标题（## 0–## 6，### 2.1–2.3，### 4.1–4.3，## 参考文献）与任务简介中的步骤 1.1 骨架字节完全一致；§0 和 §2–§6 准确包含了规定的“（Task N 填充）”锚点，包括参考文献上的“（各 Task 随写随补，Task 8 统一去重）”。
- **§1 四个小节** 1.1 合理性 / 1.2 必要性 / 1.3 可行性 / 1.4 反方与边界 全部存在，且包含了步骤 1.3 要求的所有内容要素（D3 前兆时间线、ECC 反证、带有 `is_spurious_el1_translation_fault` 挂接点的分层成本列表、带有未量化 FP/FN 标注的三重过滤器误报论证）。
- **置信度标记**：我独立统计了 §1 中的 12×【实锤】/ 13×【强推】/ 4×【假设】 = 29 —— 与实现者的声称完全一致；每个小节至少带有两个标记。
- **§1 中无 TBD/TODO/占位符**（脚本扫描已通过）。
- **案例事实与 paper_zh.md 匹配**：73 个伪转换错误 / 5 个致命错误 / 78 个事件 / 100% CPU 179 / 191 个干净核心 / 零 APEI-GHES-BERT 记录 —— 全部与 paper_zh.md 第 43–46 行以及 DIAGNOSIS_REPORT.md §2 匹配。2.6 小时的前兆引导（29.0 小时 → 31.7 小时，同一周期内有 12 个警告）与 08-14 vmcore 报告 §2（第 26–28 行）及 §10（第 149 行）相符；计算无误（113997−104485 s = 2.64 h）。
- **Git 机制**：提交 `b3be53749` 位于 `research/posparity-core179` 分支，已推送并跟踪 `origin/research/posparity-core179`；主题完全为 `docs(research): 启示一论证 — fail-fast/可观测性优先的合理性必要性可行性`；正文为空（无 Co-Authored-By）；`main` 分支不包含该提交；恰好修改了一个文件，+76 行。

唯一的瑕疵（已在实现者报告中披露）：
- **小节长度**：1.1 = 604 个汉字，1.4 = 605 个汉字，而规定为 300–600 字（1.2 = 573，1.3 = 467）。超出了 4–5 个字符（约 0.7%）， disclosed；属于技术上的微小违规，而非实质性违规。

## (2) 任务质量：已批准（有小问题；无严重或重要问题）

**无虚假信号。** 我测试的每一个数字都可以追溯到可访问的来源：从 10x-escapes PDF（已完整下载，20 页）中验证了 0.5%/5,000 DPM，100–500 DPM 工业目标，约 1,000 DPM SDC，49%/29%/10% 检测分裂，CCKC ≥80%/≥5 次崩溃/≥3 个不同堆栈/30 天，>70% 已确认，<10% 误报，以及 fail-stop “这些假设今天都不成立”的引文；从 fleetscanner PDF 中验证了 93%/23%/≈40 亿集群秒数；从 mcelog 页面中验证了 mcelog 触发器引文、“最后一个正在运行的核心”警告以及泄漏桶（leaky-bucket）阈值；从 infradead 镜像中验证了 `mce=tolerancelevel` 0–3 / 默认为 1；从 Stolte arXiv PDF 中验证了 ISO 26262 安全状态措辞（含第 1 部分 3.131 引用）。

**诚实修正本身是准确的** —— 我独立重新验证了它们：DBLP 仅记录了 “Silent Data Corruptions at Scale” 的 CoRR 条目（加上实现者正确引用的 IOLTS 2023 主题演讲 DOI），我复现了 usenix.org/conference/atc21/presentation/dixit → 404 的错误；fleetscanner 仅在 DBLP 上有 CoRR；SiliFuzz 仅有 CoRR 条目且未出现在 DBLP 的 MICRO 2022 会议记录页面中（检查了 84 个标题 —— 它从未在正式场合发表过）；HotOS'21 和 Farron SOSP'23 的 DOI 已确认。HotOS 中“每几千台机器就有几个善变核心（a few mercurial cores per several thousand machines）”的引文无法直接从 ACM 获取（机器人拦截，与报告一致），但已通过网络搜索得到证实。

1. **较小 — vmcore 章节指针偏差了两个** (POSITIONAL_PARITY_RESEARCH.md:21, :27, :74)：08-14 vmcore 报告中的“§7 风险面”引用实际上是 §9 影响与风险（该报告第 142 行），“§9 下线命令”实际上是 §10 处置建议（第 147 行）。这些引文是逐字真实的，且路径正确，但指针指向了错误的章节（同一报告中的 §2 和 §5 指针是正确的）。
2. **较小 — 一个【实锤】标记的主张超出了其自身的论据范围** (第 21 行，§1.2)：“五次致命崩溃的数据通路本就未被 ECC 覆盖”被标记为【实锤】，但其自身的标记文本承认零记录意味着“未被覆盖”或“未被检查” —— 根据文档自己的约定（实锤 = 命令可复现），该从句并非命令可复现。将其改写为析取命题（实际起支撑作用的断言 —— 对软件而言零信号 —— 是“实锤”稳固的）。
3. **较小 — 72/73 的归属不准确** (第 35 行，§1.4)：“72/73 目标为静态长生命周期映射”引用了 paper_zh.md §3.4，但该节实际上说全部 73 个都针对静态线性映射；72/73 这个数字的真正来源是 MICROARCH_SUPPLEMENT.md:78。该数字是两者中较保守的一个，且 MICROARCH_SUPPLEMENT 在同一小节的其他地方有被引用 —— 只有括号内的归属不够严密。
4. **较小 — 参考文献 [6] 混淆了 mcelog 页面** (第 71 行)：config.html 上的 "ce-error-threshold = 10/24h" 属于 [dimm] 部分，而“泄漏桶（leaky-bucket）”算法是在 triggers.html 上描述的，而不是 config.html。URL 和机制都是真实的。
5. **较小 — §1.2 末尾的断言未标记** (第 23 行)：“fail-silent … 绝不是整机级的容许稳态”跟在前一句的【强推】标记之后，而没有包含自己的标记，这在“每条主张挂证据等级”的要求下属于边缘情况。
6. **较小 — 不一致的成本对冲**：§1.3(a) 指出“近零边际成本”，而 §1.3(b) 指出“零算力开销” —— 这是同一个未量化的开销；根据诚信规则，应始终保持一致的量级/未量化表述（量化明确属于任务 6；可以加上一个前向指针）。

给下游任务的信息性说明（本身非缺陷）：
- 仓库的 08-26 报告记录了第 6 次崩溃和更新的总计（88 个事件 = 82 个警告 + 6 个错误，100% CPU 179，且记录了 ERRIDR/ERX 架构错误节点扫描也为静默）。§1 正确遵循了任务简介指定的 paper_zh.md 73/5/78 数据集；第 6 次崩溃只会增强可避免性的论点，但任务 7 可能需要进行协调。
- paper_zh.md §8 本身的参考文献列表保留了未经验证的会议归属（ATC'21/OSDI'22/MICRO'22）；实现者的会议降级修正为未来 paper_zh.md 的编辑提供了模板。

**⚠️ 无法从 diff 中验证（通过其他方式验证或仅作佐证）：**
- “ATC'21 议程 67 篇 presentation 无此文” —— 我没有重新枚举完整的会议程序页面；仅通过 DBLP (CoRR-only) 加上我复现的 404 错误进行佐证。
- HotOS'21 ACM PDF 直接读取（机器人拦截） —— 引文通过网络搜索得到佐证，与文档披露的处理方式相同。
- ISO OBP 直接获取（Cloudflare 拦截） —— 通过文档本身引用为转引的 Stolte PDF 进行了验证。
- fleetscanner PDF 插图文件名（"SELSE2022_*"）和 Dixit PDF 所属机构行 —— 未由我重新提取；非支撑性内容。

**结论：已批准。** 规范符合，机制正确，来源真实，诚信修正可独立验证。这六个小问题值得在触及 §1 的后续任务中进行一次性清理，但均不影响任何结论。

5. **较小 — §1.2 末尾的断言未标记** (第 23 行)：“fail-silent … 绝不是整机级的容许稳态”跟在前一句的【强推】标记之后，而没有包含自己的标记，这在“每条主张挂证据等级”的要求下属于边缘情况。

You are implementing Task 2 of a research plan in the repo /home/sdc/wangxu/gem5-fi (branch `research/posparity-core179` is already checked out — work on it; do NOT switch to main).

**Read this first — it is your requirements, with exact content to use verbatim:** /home/sdc/wangxu/gem5-fi/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-02-positional-parity-research/task-2-brief.md

Also read: the report's current state (POSITIONAL_PARITY_RESEARCH.md), and paper_zh.md §3.2/§6.2 for the case facts you must anchor to.

**Key requirements (details in the brief):**
1. **§2.1 合理性 — the mathematical core.** Prove the ECC-blindness proposition: for any linear block code with parity-check matrix H, if a byte-lane permutation σ≠id misroutes data AND check bits in lockstep, the syndrome is permuted too (s' = P_σ·s = 0 iff s = 0) — ECC is structurally blind to Hamming-distance-0 lane swaps. Give the matrix derivation (3-5 lines, column-permutation commutation). Then the positional-tag detection principle: per-lane tag T_i = L_i ^ popcount1(data[i]) with L_i = (i+1)&7 (bijection on 8 lanes — the constants {0..7} are pairwise distinct, so any rotation k≠0 forces L_i ≠ L_{(i+k)%8} for all i, detection probability exactly 1, data-independent). Honest scoping: D2 (address MSB stuck-at-zero) is bit-level, ordinary parity detects it; positional tags are NOT for D2. Aggregate word W: BEWARE — a pure-XOR aggregate word is permutation-invariant (W'⊕W = 0 under rotation, because XOR commutes with permutation); position-anchoring must use a NON-commutative mix (e.g., per-lane weighted mod-256 addition). This XOR-invariance finding is a core theoretical contribution of the report — present it prominently in §2.1.
2. **§2.2 必要性 — AVF angle:** fill-buffer merge stage / load-return mux are high-AVF (output directly written to architectural registers, high probability used as pointer — the case's `__per_cpu_offset[i]→cpu_rq(i)` chain is the empirical anchor). Cite Mukherjee ISCA'03 AVF methodology (verify URL/DOI). Conclusion: deploy at load-return convergence points, not uniformly chip-wide.
3. **§2.3 可行性与反方:** (i) precedent lineage table — PCI/PCIe byte-lane parity (PAR signal), DDR4 per-byte-lane CRC/DBI, T10 DIX incrementing-tag, UCIe 1.1 die-to-die CRC — each with verified URL, framing "migration to intra-CPU datapaths, not invention"; (ii) three counter-arguments addressed head-on: CRC-replacement (timing depth: serial CRC-64 ~64 stages vs per-byte 3-4 parallel XOR levels + the permutation-invariance trap), DMR-replacement (area orders of magnitude), single-case-extrapolation (the §3.2 exhaustive bit-flip falsification is forensic fact, but statistical basis for a design rule is thin — tag 【强推】, cite arXiv:2508.01786's "new detection experiments needed"); (iii) boundary — stale-line replay needs an origin/source tag (fill-buffer slot ID), out of scope, mirrors paper §6.2's own boundary statement.
4. Every claim confidence-tagged 【实锤】/【强推】/【假设】 per the repo convention (see the existing §1 for style/density). Chinese prose, English technical terms inline.
5. Commit on `research/posparity-core179` with message `docs(research): 启示二论证 — 位置锚定校验的数学合理性/AVF必要性/可行性反方`, push, no Co-Authored-By trailer.
6. Honesty: every citation needs a checkable URL/DOI (verify via WebSearch/WebFetch; do not fabricate). If a precedent's details can't be verified, say so. Do not quantify RTL area/power as fact — they are 【假设】/量级估算.

**Interfaces produced (Task 4/6 depend on these — keep them consistent):** the tag spec T_i = L_i ^ popcount1(data[i]), L_i = (i+1)&7, tagWidth=3, aggregate word must be the non-commutative (mod-256 weighted addition) variant; the XOR-invariance derivation must be complete enough for Task 6 to reference.

**Report contract:** Write your full report to /home/sdc/wangxu/gem5-fi/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-02-positional-parity-research/task-2-report.md: what you wrote, verified URLs (each with what it confirmed), commit hash, concerns. Return ONLY: status, commit hash, one-line summary, concerns.

## 2. 任务质量：**已批准** (问题分类如下)

### 数学验证（本人独立重推导，非执行者的脚本）

我从零开始重新实现了每一个数值断言；**全部确认无误**：

- **双射**：L = {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,0}，8 个不同的值。PASS。
- **锁步标签检出概率精确为 1，与数据无关**：在 200,000 次随机数据×旋转中 0 次逃逸；在相邻换位下 0/100,000 次；**在固定的对抗性数据上穷举所有 8! = 40,320 种排列 — 唯独恒等置换可以逃逸**。代数推导无懈可击：popcount 项在两边抵消，当且仅当 L_i = L_{σ(i)} ⟺ i = σ(i) 时匹配。报告相对于简报中 "1 − 2^(−tag_width)" 公式的改进是正确的 — 该界限适用于缺乏两两不同常数的设计。
- **纯 XOR 聚合字置换不变性 (W'⊕W=0)**：在 28,000 次旋转**和** 28,000 次任意排列下 0 次检出。定理成立；结论 (a)–(c) 遵循逻辑。这确实是一个真实的理论发现，且报告将其突出显示是当之无愧的。
- **加权 mod-256 限制**：随机数据下旋转检出率约 98.7%（报告：~98.6%）；常量数据下为 0。如实披露。
- **通道对称盲视**：在锁步旋转下，单字节奇偶校验和单字节交织 SEC 的检出率均为 0/5000。
- **整块 SEC-DED 并非盲视 — 执行者的诚实修正成立**：在整块 72 位系统 H 上进行全字锁步旋转，会产生非零校验子（伴随式），并在 5,000 次试验中有 4,980 次逃逸（约 0.4%）；仅数据旋转时为 4,983/5,000。报告中的“一般非零”是准确的限定表述。
- **快照模型预测**（任务 4 关注点 #1）：针对每个 k 的逃逸概率 2^gcd(k,8)/256 — 我推导并确认：奇数 k 时为 1/128，k=4 时为 1/16。正确，且与锁步模型做了正确的区分。这是任务 5 期望值的重要前沿信息。
- **D1 取证值**：slot[0]=0xffffcc879da2e000 ror-1-byte == 接收到的 0x00ffffcc879da2e0，精确匹配 — 案例锚点是真实的。

### 问题

**重要**
1. **聚合字规范遗漏了权重上的奇偶性约束** (报告第 60 行 vs 第 62 行的断言)。规范规定 "W = Σ_i w_i·data[i] + c_i mod 256，**w_i 两两不同**"，第 62 行声称 "聚合字 W 对数据逐位敏感（数值验证：50,000 次单比特翻转，逃逸 0 次）"。这一断言对于 XOR 形式（我验证了 0/50,000）以及*奇数*权重（0/50,000）成立，但对于所述的“两两不同”规范来说是**错误的**：在偶数权重下，单比特翻转会在 mod-256 加法中静默消失（我的测试：使用 [2,4,...,16] 时漏检率为 23%）。修复方法只需一个词：**"w_i 两两不同且均为奇数"**。缓解措施（因此重要，而非关键）：单通道标签能独立捕获所有单比特翻转，且任务 4 的原型使用的是纯 XOR W（完全敏感）。但 §2.1(ii) 是任务 6 引用的锁定交付物（"不得漂移"） — 请在任务 6 之前在报告中修复此问题，最好作为一个小的后续提交。

**次要**
2. 第 59 行："popcount1 … 1 级 XOR 树，7 个 XOR2" — 一个 8 输入的奇偶树深度为 3，而非 1。§2.3 的深度比较 (3–5 级) 仍然成立，但 "1 级" 的表述有误。
3. 第 54 行："数值验证：8 位伴随式中 2 位翻转" — 针对特定随机 H 实例；我的重新运行显示了以 ~4 为中心的分布（权重为 2 时为 174/5000）。核心论点“一般非零”是正确的；可选择重新表述为“一般非零（典型汉明重量 2–6）”。
4. 第 54 行："验证脚本与输出记录于 Task 2 工作笔记" — 仓库中没有提交此类工件（推测在未追踪的 .entire/ 转录中）。所有断言都是公式级可重现的（我已证明），但该指针引用了一个不可验证的工件。建议删除该从句或提交脚本。
5. 报告第 16 条 "页面正文为客户端渲染不可直接抓取" 的说明对于 UCIe 来说过于保守 — 我对 Wix 页面的直接 curl 获取到了服务器端 HTML 中的核心句子（"the UCIe Die-to-Die (D2D) adapter inserts flit headers and cyclic redundancy check (CRC) information into the flits, as well as CRC detection and replay mechanisms"; "Raw Mode bypasses many of the functions of UCIe, including error detection and replay"）。【强推，二手交叉】标签可以升级为直接验证；没有不诚实，只是过于谨慎。
6. 任务报告的下游注释（"Task 4's pure-XOR W is fine for the prototype"）与交付物中锁定的 "不得用纯 XOR 折叠" (第 60 行) 以及计划中锁定的 "聚合字用非交换变体" 之间存在轻微冲突。交付物本身通过分工解决了这个问题（第 68 行），且报告明确警告任务 4 的 .hh 注释不得声称 W 检测旋转 — 处理一致 — 但计划修正本应更简洁。
7. §2.3 反方一："串行 CRC-64 是 64 级 LFSR…每处理 1 位数据经过 64 级异或反馈" — 表述不严谨（64 指的是寄存器长度；每位的组合深度是抽头数量）。已标记为【假设】量级，所以可以接受。

### 引用抽查（14 个已检查来源中验证了 10 个）

- **Mukherjee AVF**: 从西北大学镜像下载了 PDF。页眉逐字记录："36th Annual International Symposium on Microarchitecture (MICRO), December 2003" — 会议名称修正正确。论文中逐字记录："the AVF of the instruction queue ranges between 14% and 47%, whereas the AVFs of the execution units range between 4% and 27%"。提取的文本中 "fill buffer" 出现 0 次 — §2.2 的【强推】范围限定是合理的。DOI 解析正常。
- **10x-escapes (arXiv:2508.01786)**: 下载了 PDF。两个引用句子的逐字确认，包括第 1 节列表中的确切措辞 "New test experiments to deeply understand the effectiveness…These new test experiments must overcome the drawbacks and pitfalls of previous industrial test experiments and case studies" 以及 "Such approaches incur large energy, execution time, and area overheads for commodity compute hardware"。1,000/5,000 DPM 数据已确认。作者列表（含 Fuller, X. Liu）与当前的 arXiv PDF 匹配。
- **Lee IJCA 9(4) 2016**: 下载了 PDF；确认所有四个引文逐字一致（"~700 XOR gates", "6 stage"/"6 stages of 2-input XOR gates", "CRC time < tCCD = 5nCK", "each XOR gate delay time to be allocated less than 120ps"），加上 x8/72-bit/8UI DDR4 映射。
- **Oracle DIX draft**: 已下载；所有三处引用均逐字确认（"protect against out-of-order and misdirected write scenarios"; "an incrementing counter seeded in the 32-byte CDB"; DIX_REF_INCREMENT 语义）。
- **RFC 793**: 直接获取；引用逐字一致。
- **Kernel IFS docs**: 直接获取；"a hardware feature to run circuit level tests on a CPU core to detect problems that are not caught by parity or ECC checks" 以及 SBAF 句子逐字确认。
- **AMD WP350**: 已下载；"The DLL adds the sequence number and Link Layer CRC (LCRC) to the packet" 逐字确认；TLP 图表标注（Sequence 12/16B, LCRC 4B）已确认。
- **PCI 2.2 PAR**: UCI 镜像 HTTP 200，无文本层（已确认 — pypdf 失败）；PC/104 镜像有一个带有 PAR 定义的文本层，但其第二子句有变体（"required by all PCI signals" vs "all PCI agents"）；报告引用的 "all PCI agents" 形式得到了多个独立来源的证实（Google Patents US5790831A, Kontron 手册）。披露准确。
- **DDR4 10-UI frame**: JESD79-4 原文受注册限制，但 10-UI/8+2 结构得到了 JESD79-4 §4.16 翻译和厂商数据表的证实；与 Lee 的表 1（8UI 数据 + CRC）一致。
- **DOIs**: 所有三个（MICRO.2003.1253181, ITCIndia…11141623, ISCA.2005.18）均 302-解析至有效的 ieeexplore 文档。

## 3. ⚠️ 无法验证的项目

1. **Intel 支持文章 000098402 直接获取** — 对我的 curl 返回了机器人拦截页面（491 字节）；内容（SAF <200 ms/core, ArrayBIST <5 ms, SBFT）仅通过网络搜索得到证实，与报告的主张相符。执行者称已通过 curl 获取；我无法重现其获取过程。
2. **JESD79-4 §4.16 规范文本** — 受注册限制；通过 Lee + 供应商数据表 + 规范翻译进行了证实（如报告所披露）。
3. **UCIe 1.1 规范主体** — 受注册限制；博客元数据已验证，正文句子实际上在我的获取中存在于服务器端 HTML 中（见“次要 #5”），但规范本身未读。
4. **ITC India 2025 (Angione) 全文** — IEEE 被机器人屏蔽；DOI/会议名称/作者仅通过搜索得到证实。
5. **执行者自己的验证脚本/输出**（"Task 2 工作笔记"） — 未提交到仓库。完全被我独立的重新实现所取代，上述所有断言均已通过该实现确认。

**底线**：承重的数学推导是正确的 — 包括执行者拒绝盲目照搬简报中过强主张的两处修正（通道对称范围界定；确定性检出优于 1−2^(−tag_width)）以及忠实的 XOR 不变性发现。在任务 6 之前需要一个单词的规范修复（奇数权重）；其他一切都是完善工作。批准。

| 3.1：8字节×256掩码穷举零命中 ↔ PEPR 偶然检测一致性 | ✅ | §3.1(ii) 互证结构，明确标注"两侧数据尺度不同但方向一致【强推】" |
| 3.2 必要性：源头治理 + 10x-escapes 系统级诊断闭环 | ✅ | §3.2(i) 反证 + Table 4 88%；§3.2(ii) Observation 4 闭环（test gap fixed 仅 18%） |

| 3.3(iv) 三级防线成本表 | ✅ | §3.3(iv) 表格，时长/停核代价/覆盖边界/出处四列俱全 |

**差距**：无强制性差距。

## 2. 数字一致性 — 独立复核（我亲自下载并提取了原始 PDF）

**PEPR ITC'22（从 https://wadmes.github.io/cv/raw/ITC22.pdf 下载，727KB/10页）— 全部匹配：**
- Table V 严格评价：4.8% / 8.2% / 83.4% / 100%（32,723 中的 1,579 / 2,688 / 27,303 / 32,723）✓
- Table IV 宽松评价：18.7% / 30.9% / 91.6% / 100% ✓
- 摘要 "up to 92% of TIC defects being detected fortuitously"（最多 92% 的 TIC 缺陷被偶然检测到）✓；摘要/正文 "over 30,000 14nm failing chips"（超过 30,000 片 14nm 失效芯片）✓
- Table III：176/200/220/523,863 向量；0.5/2.3/4.0/9,568.7 h ✓；523,863/176 = 2,976.5× ✓
- PV 平均输入 M1-M2-M3=3（1 输出）、M3-M4-M5=6、250×250nm²=12 ✓；l=w=125、h=3、β=50nm ✓
- "intentionally made to overlap...in all three dimensions"（有意重叠...在所有三个维度上）✓；O(n²)→O(dn)、12B→1.3B 子电路、~114B→37.1B 故障、8-GPU <1h、18.7M 门 ✓
- 结论节 "Moving forward...we plan to incorporate timing-dependent and sequence-dependent defects...voxel collapsing have to be re-examined"（展望未来...我们计划纳入时序依赖和序列依赖的缺陷...必须重新审视体素折叠）✓（省略号使用正确）
- 47 例（0.14%）全桥接、4 例超 125nm（最大 184nm）、平均 10 分钟/例、初始 >99%、63.3% 缩减、"likely inflated"（可能被夸大）✓
- "may be applied during manufacturing testing or in the field (for systems with in-field scan testing support)"（可应用于制造测试或现场（适用于具有现场扫描测试支持的系统））✓

**10x-escapes（已下载 PDF）**：5,000 vs 100-500 DPM ✓；~1,000 DPM ✓；Table 4 12%/29%/49%/10%（479/1099/1886/393 每百万）✓；NTF 36%/ELF 29%/fixed 18%/gap 10%/damaged 7% ✓；"must be extended to target sequence- and timing-dependent defects"（必须扩展以针对序列和时序依赖的缺陷）✓ 逐字；"10-100 [Nigh 25]" + "compatible with the economics of in-field testing"（与现场测试的经济学兼容）✓；Nigh 24 ">90%...cannot be explained by the 1's and 0's"（>90%...无法用 1 和 0 来解释）✓ 逐字（第 12 页）；"Exceeding several minutes...impractical"（超过几分钟...不切实际）✓；"thoroughness is unclear"（彻底性不明确）✓；CASP 开销 1%/1%…3% ✓；DIFST/IFS/IST ✓；"in-field testing also addresses ELF"（现场测试也解决了 ELF）✓。

**SiliFuzz/fleetscanner/内核 IFS**：快照 <100 字节/微秒级/单线程/核心锁定 ✓；~500,000 快照 ✓；"Wrong results for integer, floating point and vector instructions"（整数、浮点和向量指令的错误结果）第一个列表项 ✓；Unicorn C 代码关联自认 ✓；0xCC 陷阱 ✓；fleetscanner Table 1 ≈68M/≈4B fleet-seconds/23% vs ripple ≈2.5B/月/7%/15 天 vs 5-6 个月 ✓；93% 家族覆盖率 ✓；"production experience...silicon vendors"（生产经验...硅供应商）✓。内核 IFS 文档我直接抓取成功：SAF "ALL THREADS...up to 200 milliseconds"（所有线程...最长 200 毫秒）✓、SBAF "mimics the manufacturing screening environment...DFT observation sites...hundreds of milliseconds (100-200 ms)"（模拟制造筛选环境...DFT 观测点...数百毫秒 (100-200 毫秒）) ✓。

**paper_zh "≤95%" 的处理**：paper_zh.md:249 称"传统指标合计的最高偶然检测率亦不超过 95%"，该数字在 PEPR PDF 中不存在（最接近的是摘要 92% 与 Table IV 并集 91.6%）。报告采用摘要逐字数字 92% 并以 Nigh 24 ">90%" 互证——**所用数字是正确且经原文核实的**，但未按报告自身惯例加"诚实注记"说明与 paper_zh 的 95% 存在出入（对比：Mukherjee ISCA→MICRO、SiliFuzz MICRO→arXiv 均有显式注记）。见 Minor (a)。

## 3. 任务质量：**已批准**

问题分类：

**严重**：无。

**重要**：无。

**次要**：
- (a) **95%→92% 静默替换**：§3.1(ii) 使用核实后的 92% 替代 paper_zh §6.3 的"≤95%"，数字本身正确，但缺少报告其他地方对 paper_zh 引用更正时一贯使用的诚实注记（诚实注记）。建议任务 8 补一句说明。
- (b) **§3.2(i) "成本低至少一个数量级"**：断言"至少 10×"而其标签自己承认"具体倍数未量化"——所用 Table 4 原文只支持"significantly increase"（显著增加），不支持量化下界。建议弱化为"显著低于"。
- (c) **跨节不一致（非本任务缺陷，任务 8 需处理）**：§2.3 反方三仍使用已被 MICROARCH_SUPPLEMENT §2.2 明确撤回的 2⁻⁵⁸ 数字（"随机命中概率 ~2⁻⁵⁸"），而 §3/参考文献 [31] 正确回避了它。两节对同一撤回数字的处理不一致。
- (d) **Nigh 24 引文的节号定位**："§3.2.1" 的节界在文本提取中无法精确钉死（引文在第 12 页，逐字无误）；低风险。

**值得表扬**：D1 状态半的诚实边界处理是典范——前言、§3.3(ii) 专节（含 PEPR 结论节与 10x 论文双逐字引文、IC-PEPR 延伸方向为 intra-cell 而非时序的佐证）、成本表行、边界总结四处一致，且把 paper_zh 自己的"at-speed 扫描 fill-buffer 合并级"建议主动降级为【假设】——这是对源论文自身主张的诚实降级，超出最低要求。编号连续性（[22]-[31]）、标签密度、边界总结风格与 §1/§2 完全一致。

## 4. ⚠️ 无法验证的项目

1. **Intel 支持页 000098402 直接抓取**：我同样被 Akamai 403 拒绝。SAF <200ms/核、ArrayBIST <5ms、SBFT <200ms 经 Web 检索交叉核实（多源引用 Intel 原文），且 SAF 200ms 有 kernel 文档直接佐证（我已直读）。报告标注【强推，二手交叉】处理恰当——仅 ArrayBIST/SBFT 两个数字依赖二手。
2. **ITC India 2025 全文**：IEEE 反爬。摘要经 Semantic Scholar API 核实（我独立复现，摘要全文与报告引文逐字一致）；论文内部方法学细节未核。报告仅引用摘要级主张——诚实。
3. **IC-PEPR (ITC 2025) 全文**：DOI/DBLP 记录核实（conf/itc/NighPLMB25），"延伸方向为 intra-cell"主要依据标题与 10x 论文引述语境，全文未读。
4. **EDN LOS 文章**：反爬，我未独立复核（报告标注二手交叉）。
5. **fleetscanner 的 DBLP 无收录记录**：与任务 1 发现一致，但我的 DBLP 复查因搜索怪癖未能得到确定性的否定结果（返回了其他论文）。
6. **10x 论文第 11 页**：实现者报告提取失败；我本次下载提取正常（20 页），且 §3 承重引文均位于第 7-8/10/12 页，已逐字核实——该问题不影响任何已写入 §3 的主张。

**结论：已批准。** 所有核心数字经我对原始 PDF 的独立复核全部命中，git 机制全合规，诚实边界处理到位。四个 Minor 项均不阻塞，(a)(c) 建议转给任务 8 去重时统一处理。

**差距**：无强制性差距。

## 2. 数字一致性 — 独立复核（我亲自下载并提取了原始 PDF）

**PEPR ITC'22（从 https://wadmes.github.io/cv/raw/ITC22.pdf 下载，727KB/10页）— 全部匹配：**
- Table V 严格评价：4.8% / 8.2% / 83.4% / 100%（32,723 中的 1,579 / 2,688 / 27,303 / 32,723）✓
- Table IV 宽松评价：18.7% / 30.9% / 91.6% / 100% ✓
- 摘要 "up to 92% of TIC defects being detected fortuitously"（最多 92% 的 TIC 缺陷被偶然检测到）✓；摘要/正文 "over 30,000 14nm failing chips"（超过 30,000 片 14nm 失效芯片）✓
- Table III：176/200/220/523,863 向量；0.5/2.3/4.0/9,568.7 h ✓；523,863/176 = 2,976.5× ✓
- PV 平均输入 M1-M2-M3=3（1 输出）、M3-M4-M5=6、250×250nm²=12 ✓；l=w=125、h=3、β=50nm ✓
- "intentionally made to overlap...in all three dimensions"（有意重叠...在所有三个维度上）✓；O(n²)→O(dn)、12B→1.3B 子电路、~114B→37.1B 故障、8-GPU <1h、18.7M 门 ✓
- 结论节 "Moving forward...we plan to incorporate timing-dependent and sequence-dependent defects...voxel collapsing have to be re-examined"（展望未来...我们计划纳入时序依赖和序列依赖的缺陷...必须重新审视体素折叠）✓（省略号使用正确）
- 47 例（0.14%）全桥接、4 例超 125nm（最大 184nm）、平均 10 分钟/例、初始 >99%、63.3% 缩减、"likely inflated"（可能被夸大）✓
- "may be applied during manufacturing testing or in the field (for systems with in-field scan testing support)"（可应用于制造测试或现场（适用于具有现场扫描测试支持的系统））✓

**10x-escapes（已下载 PDF）**：5,000 vs 100-500 DPM ✓；~1,000 DPM ✓；Table 4 12%/29%/49%/10%（479/1099/1886/393 每百万）✓；NTF 36%/ELF 29%/fixed 18%/gap 10%/damaged 7% ✓；"must be extended to target sequence- and timing-dependent defects"（必须扩展以针对序列和时序依赖的缺陷）✓ 逐字；"10-100 [Nigh 25]" + "compatible with the economics of in-field testing"（与现场测试的经济学兼容）✓；Nigh 24 ">90%...cannot be explained by the 1's and 0's"（>90%...无法用 1 和 0 来解释）✓ 逐字（第 12 页）；"Exceeding several minutes...impractical"（超过几分钟...不切实际）✓；"thoroughness is unclear"（彻底性不明确）✓；CASP 开销 1%/1%…3% ✓；DIFST/IFS/IST ✓；"in-field testing also addresses ELF"（现场测试也解决了 ELF）✓。

**SiliFuzz/fleetscanner/内核 IFS**：快照 <100 字节/微秒级/单线程/核心锁定 ✓；~500,000 快照 ✓；"Wrong results for integer, floating point and vector instructions"（整数、浮点和向量指令的错误结果）第一个列表项 ✓；Unicorn C 代码关联自认 ✓；0xCC 陷阱 ✓；fleetscanner Table 1 ≈68M/≈4B fleet-seconds/23% vs ripple ≈2.5B/月/7%/15 天 vs 5-6 个月 ✓；93% 家族覆盖率 ✓；"production experience...silicon vendors"（生产经验...硅供应商）✓。内核 IFS 文档我直接抓取成功：SAF "ALL THREADS...up to 200 milliseconds"（所有线程...最长 200 毫秒）✓、SBAF "mimics the manufacturing screening environment...DFT observation sites...hundreds of milliseconds (100-200 ms)"（模拟制造筛选环境...DFT 观测点...数百毫秒 (100-200 毫秒）) ✓。

**paper_zh "≤95%" 的处理**：paper_zh.md:249 称"传统指标合计的最高偶然检测率亦不超过 95%"，该数字在 PEPR PDF 中不存在（最接近的是摘要 92% 与 Table IV 并集 91.6%）。报告采用摘要逐字数字 92% 并以 Nigh 24 ">90%" 互证——**所用数字是正确且经原文核实的**，但未按报告自身惯例加"诚实注记"说明与 paper_zh 的 95% 存在出入（对比：Mukherjee ISCA→MICRO、SiliFuzz MICRO→arXiv 均有显式注记）。见 Minor (a)。

## 3. 任务质量：**已批准**

问题分类：

**严重**：无。

**重要**：无。

**次要**：
- (a) **95%→92% 静默替换**：§3.1(ii) 使用核实后的 92% 替代 paper_zh §6.3 的"≤95%"，数字本身正确，但缺少报告其他地方对 paper_zh 引用更正时一贯使用的诚实注记（诚实注记）。建议任务 8 补一句说明。
- (b) **§3.2(i) "成本低至少一个数量级"**：断言"至少 10×"而其标签自己承认"具体倍数未量化"——所用 Table 4 原文只支持"significantly increase"（显著增加），不支持量化下界。建议弱化为"显著低于"。
- (c) **跨节不一致（非本任务缺陷，任务 8 需处理）**：§2.3 反方三仍使用已被 MICROARCH_SUPPLEMENT §2.2 明确撤回的 2⁻⁵⁸ 数字（"随机命中概率 ~2⁻⁵⁸"），而 §3/参考文献 [31] 正确回避了它。两节对同一撤回数字的处理不一致。
- (d) **Nigh 24 引文的节号定位**："§3.2.1" 的节界在文本提取中无法精确钉死（引文在第 12 页，逐字无误）；低风险。

**值得表扬**：D1 状态半的诚实边界处理是典范——前言、§3.3(ii) 专节（含 PEPR 结论节与 10x 论文双逐字引文、IC-PEPR 延伸方向为 intra-cell 而非时序的佐证）、成本表行、边界总结四处一致，且把 paper_zh 自己的"at-speed 扫描 fill-buffer 合并级"建议主动降级为【假设】——这是对源论文自身主张的诚实降级，超出最低要求。编号连续性（[22]-[31]）、标签密度、边界总结风格与 §1/§2 完全一致。

## 4. ⚠️ 无法验证的项目

1. **Intel 支持页 000098402 直接抓取**：我同样被 Akamai 403 拒绝。SAF <200ms/核、ArrayBIST <5ms、SBFT <200ms 经 Web 检索交叉核实（多源引用 Intel 原文），且 SAF 200ms 有 kernel 文档直接佐证（我已直读）。报告标注【强推，二手交叉】处理恰当——仅 ArrayBIST/SBFT 两个数字依赖二手。
2. **ITC India 2025 全文**：IEEE 反爬。摘要经 Semantic Scholar API 核实（我独立复现，摘要全文与报告引文逐字一致）；论文内部方法学细节未核。报告仅引用摘要级主张——诚实。
3. **IC-PEPR (ITC 2025) 全文**：DOI/DBLP 记录核实（conf/itc/NighPLMB25），"延伸方向为 intra-cell"主要依据标题与 10x 论文引述语境，全文未读。
4. **EDN LOS 文章**：反爬，我未独立复核（报告标注二手交叉）。
5. **fleetscanner 的 DBLP 无收录记录**：与任务 1 发现一致，但我的 DBLP 复查因搜索怪癖未能得到确定性的否定结果（返回了其他论文）。
6. **10x 论文第 11 页**：实现者报告提取失败；我本次下载提取正常（20 页），且 §3 承重引文均位于第 7-8/10/12 页，已逐字核实——该问题不影响任何已写入 §3 的主张。

**结论：已批准。** 所有核心数字经我对原始 PDF 的独立复核全部命中，git 机制全合规，诚实边界处理到位。四个 Minor 项均不阻塞，(a)(c) 建议转给任务 8 去重时统一处理。

# Task 4 Review — CHAOSPosParity validator (commit cd52c4052)

## 1. Spec compliance

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| Files: 4 new in `CHAOS/gem5/src/cpu/o3/CHAOSPosParity/` + synced `CHAOS/CHAOSPosParity/` copy | ✅ `diff -r` clean — copies identical |
| cpu.hh hook (~4 lines, mirroring lsqFwd: fwd-decl + member + accessors) | ✅ cpu.hh:97-99, 507-514, exact mirror of the addrPath pattern |
| lsq_unit.cc insertion (tag before corrupt, verify after, same buffer, before packet) | ✅ lsq_unit.cc:1500-1526; only `corrupt()` call site in the tree, so hook coverage is complete |
| Minimal `--posparity`/`--posparity-action` in runner, default `count` | ✅ o3_chaos_smoke.py:74-75, 187-197; tagWidth=3 wired |
| Locked stats names / params | ✅ all four stats appear as `system.posparity.<name>`; `tagWidth=3`, `action=count\|panic`, `rngSeed` |
| One commit on `research/posparity-core179`, no Co-Authored-By, pushed | ✅ `rev-list 2fb2f0703..cd52c4052 --count` = 1; origin in sync; 0 trailer matches |
| Build clean | ✅ I re-ran a forced rebuild (`touch CHAOSPosParity.cc` + scons): 0 `warning:|error:` lines; only pre-existing capstone/png/HDF5 host notices |
| Golden run (validator ON, no injection) | ✅ Reproduced **exactly**: `fails=0`, `numTagged=529`, `numVerified=529`, `numMismatches=0`, tick 31011000 — identical to the report |
| Injection regression (validator absent) | ✅ in substance: `grep -c posparity stats.txt` → 0; `numStructuralByteLaneSkew=1`, hook called 529×, gem5 stable. ⚠️ but the quoted `ptr_corrupt=1` is a nondeterministic draw — see Important #3 |
| Detection-path proofs (skew→1, bit-flip→1 via W, panic abort) | ✅ all reproduced (panic at `CHAOSPosParity.cc:100`, rc=134; bit-flip 1/1; all_zero 1/1) |
| **Locked detection semantics: rotation → per-lane tags, EXACTLY 100%, "identity is the only escape, proven by exhaustive 8! enumeration"** | ❌ **FALSE for the implemented wiring — see Critical #1** |
| W permutation-invariance NOT claimed as rotation detection | ✅ correctly stated (.hh:49-52, .py:12-14) — W's invariance is stated and W is scoped to bit-flip backstop only |
| Size-symmetry of tag/verify truncation | ✅ both clamp to 16; `verify` additionally clamps to `tag_snapshot_size`; no asymmetry bug at size>16 |
| laneConst = (i+1)&((1<<w)-1), bijection argument | ✅ formula correct, bijection claim correct — but irrelevant to the comparison (see #1) |
| Single-snapshot limitation declared in .hh | ✅ .hh:76-81 |
| numTagged=529/500 plausible | ✅ 1 checked forward per iter + ~29 startup/libc forwards; cross-checked: equals `numHooksCalled=529` in injector-only runs |

## 2. Task quality: **NOT approved** — 1 Critical

### Critical 1 — The central detection claim is mathematically false for the implemented code, and is empirically falsified in-simulator

**Claim** (CHAOSPosParity.hh:40-47, repeated at .py:8-13, lsq_unit.cc:1518, the commit message, and task-4-report.md:22/163): rotations are caught by per-lane tags with "probability EXACTLY 1 … The ONLY escape is the identity permutation — verified exhaustively over all 8! = 40,320 permutations. Data-independent."

**Why it is false.** In the implemented snapshot comparison, `laneConst(i)` appears on *both* sides and cancels:

- `tag()` (CHAOSPosParity.cc:72): `tag_snapshot[i] = L_i ^ p(d[i])`
- `verify()` (cc:89-90): `t = L_i ^ p(d'[i]); if (t != tag_snapshot[i])` → mismatch ⟺ `p(d'[i]) != p(d[i])`

The lane constants are mathematically inert; the per-lane check degenerates to **plain per-byte parity comparison** — precisely the conventional mechanism the paper's §6.2 argument dismisses. Rotation by k escapes iff it maps equal-parity lanes onto each other: probability **2^gcd(k,8)/256** (1/128 for odd k, 1/16 for k=4) — exactly the *snapshot-model* prediction in Task 2's report (Concern 1, task-2-report.md:79), which the implementer's report **inverts** at line 163 ("Task-2's alternative 2^gcd(k,8)/256 escape figure described a different (lockstep tag-arrival comparison) model and does NOT apply here" — backwards: 2^gcd(k,8)/256 *is* the snapshot figure; exactly-1 *is* the lockstep figure). The .hh derivation's premise "the sender stored L_sigma(i) ^ p(d_sigma(i))" (hh:43-44) describes a comparison against `tag_snapshot[σ(i)]` — the code compares against `tag_snapshot[i]`; the data permutation does not permute the snapshot array. The cited 8! = 40,320 exhaustive verification belongs to the lockstep comparison, which this code does not implement.

**Empirical proof (all real, run by me):**

1. Hand-simulation of the exact code: `d = {01,02,04,08,10,20,40,80}` (all bytes odd parity) escapes **all 7 rotations** (`verify` → false, W also equal).
2. C replica of the exact tag/verify: random-data escape rates 0.72% (k=1,3,5,7), 1.57% (k=2,6), 6.27% (k=4) — matching 2^gcd(k,8)/256.
3. Exhaustive 8! on the *snapshot* comparison, fixed datum: **576 non-identity permutations escape** (= 4!·4!, the parity-partition preservers; 0 escape under the lockstep comparison).
4. **In-simulator falsification**: probe storing the uniform-parity constant `0x0102040810204080` (532 forwards/500 iters, volatile reload), `--lsq-structural byte_lane_skew --lsq-skew 1 --lsq-fwd-prob 0.05 --seed 13 --posparity`:
   ```
   system.lsqfi.numStructuralByteLaneSkew   1
   system.posparity.numMismatches           0
   guest: intact=499/500
   ```
   A real D1 injection was delivered on the checked forward (the guest itself saw `x != v`), and the validator **missed it completely**. (Seeds 11/14/15 detected — pointer-ish/mixed data escapes only at the ~1/128 rate; seed 13 is the adversarial-data case the "Data-independent" claim says cannot exist.)

**Consequences.** The research artifact's core §6.2 property (deterministic position-anchored rotation detection where parity/ECC give 0) is *not* demonstrated by this wiring; Task 5 has been explicitly instructed (report:163) to expect a 100% measured rate that will not hold on adversarial data; Task 6 would cite a false verified claim; the commit message permanently asserts it. Under the repo's absolute honesty mandate this cannot be merged as-is.

**Fix direction (either):** (a) correct all comments/commit-report/Task-5 guidance to the true snapshot-model rate (1 − 2^gcd(k,8)/256, data-dependent), citing Task 2 Concern 1; or (b) if prob-1 is to be demonstrated, the check must actually anchor position — per Task 2 §2.1(iii) any pure-XOR mixing cancels (the XOR-invariance theorem applies to the per-lane tags too: `p(x^c) = p(x)^p(c)`), so it needs non-commutative mixing (e.g., the weighted mod-256 aggregate Task 2 already specified as the rotation-sensitive alternative) or a wiring where tags travel with the data (lockstep).

### Important

2. **All_zero figure wrong** — CHAOSPosParity.hh:53 claims "probability 1 − 2^-24". Actual escape for this code: all 8 bytes even parity (2^-8) ∧ XOR of all bytes = 0 given all even (2^-7, the even-parity bytes form a 7-dim subspace) = **2^-15**. Monte Carlo on the exact code: 54/2,000,000 ≈ 2^-15.2 ✓. (Inherited from the brief's reasoning, but the .hh asserts it as verified.)

3. **"deterministic given --seed default 0" is false** (task-4-report.md:163). CHAOSLSQFwd.cc:32 seeds from `std::random_device` when seed==0, so every quoted injection run is nondeterministic. Re-running the report's *identical* D1-without-validator command I drew `ptr_corrupt=0 fails=0` (injection hit an unchecked forward; guest passed) vs the quoted `ptr_corrupt=1 fails=1`. The regression's substance holds (validator absent → 0 posparity stats, D1 machinery unchanged), but the quoted output is one draw, and Task 5 must use nonzero `--seed` or its sweeps won't be reproducible.

### Minor

4. `tag_snapshot_vaddr` (hh:87) is written, never read — dead state (harmless, no warning).
5. The 16-byte snapshot cap silently leaves lanes ≥16 unverified for any forwarded size > 16 (possible with wide SIMD loads); unreachable in this workload (FwdSize=8), but the cap is undocumented as a coverage limit.
6. cpu.hh hook placed after CHAOSAddrPath rather than between `getLSQFwd` and CHAOSAddrPath as the brief sketched — cosmetic; the mirror-pattern requirement is fully met.

## 3. ⚠️ Cannot-verify

- **Exact quoted tick/cycle numbers of the implementer's runs (a)/(b)/(c)** — panic tick 13762500 vs my 3599000, injection cycle 37611 vs my 25158: not reproducible because seed-0 runs use `random_device`. All *qualitative* outcomes reproduced (golden exactly; skew→1 mismatch; bit-flip→1; all_zero→1; panic rc=134 at the injection tick).
- **Pre-task byte-identical D1 chain** — would require rebuilding from 2fb2f0703; supported indirectly (nullptr short-circuit is trivially inert; `grep -c posparity` → 0; `numHooksCalled=529` matches the validator run's `numTagged=529`).
- **Build-environment narrative** (1,849 root-owned artifacts relocated; ~11.6 MB `*.rootjunk` remains) — I confirmed 10 root-owned files remain in two `*.rootjunk` dirs outside scons's target set and that the build completes clean; the historical count/operation can't be re-verified. No source-tree or git impact.
- **Who ran the original 8! = 40,320 exhaustive check and against which comparison** — progress.md:13 attributes it to "the reviewer"; my own exhaustive run shows it can only have been the lockstep comparison (0 non-identity escapes there vs 576 in the snapshot wiring), so the attribution error in the inherited claim, not the enumeration itself, is the root of Critical #1.

**Bottom line:** engineering, wiring, build, regression, and git mechanics are all clean and reproduced; but the prototype's central mathematical claim (rotation detection exactly 1, data-independent, only identity escapes) is false for the implemented snapshot comparison — the lane constants cancel, reducing the per-lane check to conventional parity — and I falsified it live in the simulator (1 skew injected, 0 mismatches, on uniform-parity data). Requires rework of the claim (or of the check) before Task 5 builds on it.

### Critical 1 — The central detection claim is mathematically false for the implemented code, and is empirically falsified in-simulator

**Claim** (CHAOSPosParity.hh:40-47, repeated at .py:8-13, lsq_unit.cc:1518, the commit message, and task-4-report.md:22/163): rotations are caught by per-lane tags with "probability EXACTLY 1 … The ONLY escape is the identity permutation — verified exhaustively over all 8! = 40,320 permutations. Data-independent."

**Why it is false.** In the implemented snapshot comparison, `laneConst(i)` appears on *both* sides and cancels:

- `tag()` (CHAOSPosParity.cc:72): `tag_snapshot[i] = L_i ^ p(d[i])`
- `verify()` (cc:89-90): `t = L_i ^ p(d'[i]); if (t != tag_snapshot[i])` → mismatch ⟺ `p(d'[i]) != p(d[i])`

The lane constants are mathematically inert; the per-lane check degenerates to **plain per-byte parity comparison** — precisely the conventional mechanism the paper's §6.2 argument dismisses. Rotation by k escapes iff it maps equal-parity lanes onto each other: probability **2^gcd(k,8)/256** (1/128 for odd k, 1/16 for k=4) — exactly the *snapshot-model* prediction in Task 2's report (Concern 1, task-2-report.md:79), which the implementer's report **inverts** at line 163 ("Task-2's alternative 2^gcd(k,8)/256 escape figure described a different (lockstep tag-arrival comparison) model and does NOT apply here" — backwards: 2^gcd(k,8)/256 *is* the snapshot figure; exactly-1 *is* the lockstep figure). The .hh derivation's premise "the sender stored L_sigma(i) ^ p(d_sigma(i))" (hh:43-44) describes a comparison against `tag_snapshot[σ(i)]` — the code compares against `tag_snapshot[i]`; the data permutation does not permute the snapshot array. The cited 8! = 40,320 exhaustive verification belongs to the lockstep comparison, which this code does not implement.

**Empirical proof (all real, run by me):**

1. Hand-simulation of the exact code: `d = {01,02,04,08,10,20,40,80}` (all bytes odd parity) escapes **all 7 rotations** (`verify` → false, W also equal).
2. C replica of the exact tag/verify: random-data escape rates 0.72% (k=1,3,5,7), 1.57% (k=2,6), 6.27% (k=4) — matching 2^gcd(k,8)/256.
3. Exhaustive 8! on the *snapshot* comparison, fixed datum: **576 non-identity permutations escape** (= 4!·4!, the parity-partition preservers; 0 escape under the lockstep comparison).
4. **In-simulator falsification**: probe storing the uniform-parity constant `0x0102040810204080` (532 forwards/500 iters, volatile reload), `--lsq-structural byte_lane_skew --lsq-skew 1 --lsq-fwd-prob 0.05 --seed 13 --posparity`:

**Consequences.** The research artifact's core §6.2 property (deterministic position-anchored rotation detection where parity/ECC give 0) is *not* demonstrated by this wiring; Task 5 has been explicitly instructed (report:163) to expect a 100% measured rate that will not hold on adversarial data; Task 6 would cite a false verified claim; the commit message permanently asserts it. Under the repo's absolute honesty mandate this cannot be merged as-is.

**Fix direction (either):** (a) correct all comments/commit-report/Task-5 guidance to the true snapshot-model rate (1 − 2^gcd(k,8)/256, data-dependent), citing Task 2 Concern 1; or (b) if prob-1 is to be demonstrated, the check must actually anchor position — per Task 2 §2.1(iii) any pure-XOR mixing cancels (the XOR-invariance theorem applies to the per-lane tags too: `p(x^c) = p(x)^p(c)`), so it needs non-commutative mixing (e.g., the weighted mod-256 aggregate Task 2 already specified as the rotation-sensitive alternative) or a wiring where tags travel with the data (lockstep).

### Important

2. **All_zero figure wrong** — CHAOSPosParity.hh:53 claims "probability 1 − 2^-24". # Task 5 Review — Detection-Matrix Experiment (CHAOSPosParity)

## 1. Spec compliance vs the brief

Verified against the actual API: `src/python/pybind11/event.cc:108` defines `m.def("simulate", &simulate, py::arg("ticks") = MaxTick)`; Root has no `max_tick` param in gem5 25.1. Matches the `o3_chaos_fs.py:131-136` precedent. Cannot break other users: the old `root.max_tick = ...` path always raised AttributeError (added in checkpoint `f5900ce31`, never functional). `--max-tick 0` behavior unchanged. My re-runs confirm stats are dumped on cap (`cause=simulate() limit reached`). |
| Adaptive max-tick retry | ✅ (no rate bias) | Truncates counts (excludes the crash tail) but does not bias the rate: any injection inside the window is fully tag+verify'd in the same event (`lsq_unit.cc:1494-1530`, back-to-back). The tight retry (T−100k) correctly re-includes the (T−500k, T−100k] window the coarse retry straddled. Determinism of same-seed reruns verified independently: the OFF arm's first 14 injection-log lines are byte-identical to the ON arm's. Selection effect (lethal injections excluded from count) biases *against* detection, i.e., conservative. |

**Numbers I reproduced myself (exact matches):**
- golden seed 42: `numTagged=2029 numVerified=2029 numMismatches=0`, `fails=0`
- bit_flip seed 1: `numFaultsInjected=338 numBitFlips=338 numMismatches=338`
- skew seed 4 @60M cap: `numStructuralByteLaneSkew=14 numMismatches=10`

**Escape mathematics — all implementer claims independently confirmed** (my own exhaustive C program): targets[j]=0x1000·(j+1): exactly 17/1792 = 0.949% escaping (word,k) pairs; escaping j = {1(k4), 3(k2,4,6), 5(k4), 7(all 7), 9(k4), 11(k2,4,6), 13(k4)}; single-nonzero-byte exhaustive 136/14280 with by-k {8,24,8,56,8,24,8}; MC uniform-random 0.5055%; **targets[7]=0x8000 escapes all 7 rotations hand-verified** (ror_1: ΔW1 = (w₁_1−w₁_0)·0x80 = 2·128 = 256 ≡ 0; ΔW2 = (0x59−0x5B)·128 = −256 ≡ 0); all_zero escape point (W1,W2)(zeros) = (64,192) = (0x40,0xC0) confirmed; unipar word 0x0102040810204080 mathematically detected under all 7 rotations.

## 2. Task quality: **Issues found — not approved as-is**

### Critical 1 — Arm 7 (unipar) simulator evidence is vacuous: the probe's loop was optimized away at -O2

`run_posparity.sh` builds unipar with `gcc -static -O2`. At -O2 the entire loop body (`buf[i&3]=v; x=buf[i&3]; intact+=(x==v)`) is eliminated — I disassembled the exact experiment binary (`/tmp/unipar_rebuilt`, md5-identical to my fresh rebuild of `fi_research/probes/unipar_probe.c`): `main` contains **zero memory instructions** besides the stack-frame `stp/ldp`; the loop is a bare counter and `intact` is effectively compile-time. Consequences:
- `intact=5000/5000` proves nothing — it is printed unconditionally after a spin loop.
- The 11 injections landed on glibc/loader forwards (logs show vaddrs 0x7ffffeecd8/0x7ffffef580/0x496698 — stack/libc, never `buf`), and `numTagged=29` for a "5000-iteration store/reload loop" confirms the loop never forwarded.
- The report's "unipar 对抗数据 k=1: 11/11 = 100% … 一致" and the commit message's "Critical-1 回归守护" present these runs as testing the adversarial word 0x0102040810204080. **That word never traveled the forwarding path in any arm-7 run.** The 11/11 detections are of unrelated loader/libc words.

The underlying *mathematical* claim is true (I verified all 7 rotations are detected), but the simulator evidence does not demonstrate it. Fix: build unipar with `-O0` (or make `buf` volatile / add a compiler barrier that actually forces the reload), re-run arm 7, and verify `numTagged` ≈ iters before claiming the guard.

### Critical 2 — The skew-arm escape attribution (Key Finding 2) is wrong: the escapes are glibc loader words, not the probe's targets[] constants

The report and commit message state the 4 seed-4 escapes are "探针合成金标值 targets[j]=0x1000*(j+1)". My forensics on the implementer's own debug artifacts (`/tmp/posparity_dbg_s4/lsqdbg.txt`) refutes this:

- **The probe's main loop never executed inside the captured window.** All 14 injections occur at load PCs 0x444538/0x44419c — inside glibc's `_dl_find_object_init`/`_dlfo_sort_mappings` (loader startup sort). No PC in the probe main-loop range (0x4005e4–0x40061c) appears anywhere in the 60M-tick log; the sort is still executing at tick 60000000. `targets[]` had not even been initialized in-window (no stores to the 0x49xxxx heap region from probe init).
- **The implementer's own snapshot data contradicts the attribution.** The 10 detected events' snapshot aggregates are (185,91)×6, (128,128)×3, (66,118)×1 — which decode exactly to **0x48c3c8 (RW segment start)**, **0x400000 (RE segment start)**, and **0x2 (mapping count)**: loader `_dlfo` mapping-array words. Not one targets[j]-class W-pair (e.g. 0x1000→(112,80), 0x8000→(192,64)) appears. The 4 escapes (vaddrs 0x497fc0/0x498200/0x498800/0x498940, all in the 32-byte-stride loader mapping array at 0x497f00..0x4989a0) are unidentified loader words — most plausibly 0x400000 under even k (0x400000 escapes k∈{2,4,6}; the 3 detected 0x400000 events were all odd-k, and an odd/even split of ~6 events giving 3 detected + 3 escaped fits perfectly) and/or NULL fields (all-zero words trivially escape every rotation).
- **The "14 注入 vaddr 指针值本身不逃逸任何旋转" check is a category error**: it computed W() of the *addresses* (0x48fb78, 0x497f00, …), not of the *forwarded words* (the contents at those addresses). The right computation on the actual words was never done.

What survives: the 77.8% (14/18) measurement itself is real and honestly reported; the general mathematical conclusion (single-nonzero-byte low-entropy words escape at ~0.95%, double the uniform-random rate, concentrated on ror_4) is correct — and 0x400000 *is* a single-nonzero-byte word, so the class-level story accidentally holds. But the specific mechanism claim ("escape class is the probe's synthetic constants, not the D1 pointer chain") is unfounded, and the paper-facing narrative must be corrected before Task 7 cites it.

### Important 1 — The skew-ON arms never exercised the D1 pointer chain at all

All 18 skew-arm events across all 5 seeds are loader/startup words (injection logs: 0x48fb78 count word, 0x497f00.. loader array, 0x7ffffef… startup stack). The probe's own D1 forward (stack spill of `golden_ptr` at 0x7ffffefca8, 367 events in the seed-4 OFF arm at cycles 313287–324326 ≈ ticks 156M–162M) is reachable — but only far beyond the 60M default cap. The seed-4 OFF arm survived to 173M ticks, proving a ~170M cap would have captured ~367 probe-loop skew events on the actual pointer word. Concern 1's explanation ("风暴下客户机早死 → n=18") is incorrect for seed 4: the guest did not die; the window was just too short. Note the asymmetry: the bit_flip and all_zero arms *did* complete and exercise the probe loop (367/360 of their injections at 0x7ffffefca8), which is why those arms have large n. Re-running skew seed 4 with a 170M cap is cheap and would give the skew cell real D1-chain statistics.

### Minor

1. Report says results.md is 302 lines; it is 320.
2. `--max-tick` help text still says "(Root.max_tick)" — stale after the fix.
3. Report characterizes the crash sites as "栈溢出槽/退出路径 skew" — they are the loader sort phase (imprecise, related to Critical 2).
4. Debug artifacts live at `/tmp/posparity_dbg_s4/`, not referenced in the report (they were decisive evidence and should be cited for reproducibility).
5. Panic-arm mismatch was on a libc bss word (0x496690) — fine for the fail-fast demonstration, which makes no D1-chain claim.

## 3. ⚠️ Cannot-verify items

1. **The exact words at the 4 escape events** — not logged (would need a guest-memory dump or a data DPRINTF). My 0x400000-under-even-k / NULL hypotheses are strongly inferred from the detected-snapshot pattern and the single-nonzero-byte escape set, but not proven.
2. **The implementer's incremental scons "build clean" claim** — no log; low risk since no C++ changed (commit touches only .py/.sh; gem5.opt predates the runs).
3. **Task 4's in-simulator unipar "all 7 rotations verified" claim** — outside this diff; if it used the same -O2 binary, it was equally vacuous (worth a follow-up check, since Critical 1 suggests the probe was broken from birth).
4. **The implementer's 2×10⁵ MC run** — no artifact; however my own MC reproduces the figure (0.5055%), so the number is right regardless.

## Bottom line

Mechanics, honesty of the headline deviation (77.8%), escape mathematics, runner fix, and git discipline are all solid and independently reproduced. But two load-bearing claims do not survive scrutiny: **arm 7's "11/11 adversarial-word detection" is vacuous (probe loop optimized away)**, and **Key Finding 2's attribution of the skew escapes to targets[] constants is refuted by the implementer's own debug log (they are glibc loader mapping-array words; the probe loop never ran in-window)**. Required before approval: (a) rebuild unipar at -O0 and re-run arm 7 after confirming numTagged ≈ iters; (b) correct the escape attribution in the report (and flag the commit-message claim as erroneous in a follow-up note); (c) ideally re-run skew seed 4 with a ~170M cap to measure detection on the actual D1 pointer chain.

## 2. Task quality: **Issues found — not approved as-is**

### Critical 1 — Arm 7 (unipar) simulator evidence is vacuous: the probe's loop was optimized away at -O2

`run_posparity.sh` builds unipar with `gcc -static -O2`. At -O2 the entire loop body (`buf[i&3]=v; x=buf[i&3]; intact+=(x==v)`) is eliminated — I disassembled the exact experiment binary (`/tmp/unipar_rebuilt`, md5-identical to my fresh rebuild of `fi_research/probes/unipar_probe.c`): `main` contains **zero memory instructions** besides the stack-frame `stp/ldp`; the loop is a bare counter and `intact` is effectively compile-time. - `intact=5000/5000` proves nothing — it is printed unconditionally after a spin loop.

- **The probe's main loop never executed inside the captured window.** All 14 injections occur at load PCs 0x444538/0x44419c — inside glibc's `_dl_find_object_init`/`_dlfo_sort_mappings` (loader startup sort). No PC in the probe main-loop range (0x4005e4–0x40061c) appears anywhere in the 60M-tick log; the sort is still executing at tick 60000000. `targets[]` had not even been initialized in-window (no stores to the 0x49xxxx heap region from probe init).
- **The implementer's own snapshot data contradicts the attribution.** The 10 detected events' snapshot aggregates are (185,91)×6, (128,128)×3, (66,118)×1 — which decode exactly to **0x48c3c8 (RW segment start)**, **0x400000 (RE segment start)**, and **0x2 (mapping count)**: loader `_dlfo` mapping-array words. The 4 escapes (vaddrs 0x497fc0/0x498200/0x498800/0x498940, all in the 32-byte-stride loader mapping array at 0x497f00..0x4989a0) are unidentified loader words — most plausibly 0x400000 under even k (0x400000 escapes k∈{2,4,6}; the 3 detected 0x400000 events were all odd-k, and an odd/even split of ~6 events giving 3 detected + 3 escaped fits perfectly) and/or NULL fields (all-zero words trivially escape every rotation).
- **The "14 注入 vaddr 指针值本身不逃逸任何旋转" check is a category error**: it computed W() of the *addresses* (0x48fb78, 0x497f00, …), not of the *forwarded words* (the contents at those addresses). The right computation on the actual words was never done.
